about: The GMQ card catalogue. One list for the battle, the card pop-up, the card book and the game. The battle thread owns it.

Edit this file, then run: python3 checks/battle_cards_sync.py (it copies the list into docs/battle/index.html and docs/battle/cards.html and their prototypes), then python3 checks/battle_cards_set_check.py.
Every card is a Proposal for Marc. The rules are his.

fields.id: never changes once a card exists. Saved games and Marc's picks use it.
fields.group: battle card, ship part, upgrade, or idea (an idea waits for a rule from Marc and is not in any deck).
fields.name: the name on the card
fields.rarity: common, rare or epic. Ship parts and upgrades have none yet (Marc's decision).
fields.type: attack, defence, repair, spy, guard or upgrade: the big symbol on the card. sym "dodge" changes the symbol to the dodge picture.
fields.kind: ship parts only: standard, guardian, striker or lucky (the border colour).
fields.badge: the one big number in the white circle
fields.ops: what the card does, for the battle engine. Each op names its numbers (n, parts, hp, ap).
fields.needs: only on a card with two effects: the two parts it needs
fields.pic: the picture key, one for each card
fields.picture: what the picture shows, in a few words, for the visual design thread
fields.ask: ideas only: the rule it needs from Marc

number_rule.in_words: Common: one small number. Rare: about double, or two things at once. Epic: it does something no other card does.
steps: 15 to 30; 4 or 5 for each working part; or two things
double it; round it up to the next hundred
6 to 15; 3 for each card in your hand
18 to 30; 4 for each card; or two things
8 to 15; 3 for each card in your hand
back to full (100); full shield and full parts
5 to 12 on one part; 2 or 3 on every part; share 10; move 5
15 or 20 on one part; 4 or 5 on every part; share 20 or 25; round up; move 10
bring a part back; bring every lost part back; every part to full
also: No two battle cards do the same thing.
Every rare beats every common of its kind.
Each half of a two-thing card is no bigger than a common card.
An attack card and a block card of the same size cancel.

deck_rules.source: Marc, 22 November: one Spy card in each deck; at least as many Policemen as Spies. Rules sheet section 1: a deck has no limit on size or kind.
deck_rules.own_deck: A battle with a child's own cards: every battle card they own goes in. If they own more than one Spy card, one is drawn at random to go in. If the deck has fewer Guards than Spies, the station lends a Station Guard. If they own fewer than 15 battle cards, the station lends cards from their starter pack until there are 15. [Proposal]
deck_rules.computer_deck: The computer gets a deck of the same shape: for each of the child's cards, a card of the same type and kind (common, rare, epic), drawn at random. [Proposal]

starter_pack.source: Marc, 23 November: "Every kid gets 1 spy, 1 policeman, 1 epic, and 1 rare in their space station initial 15 starter pack."

slots.why: the Spy (Marc). Common: the rare and the epic are the two below. [Proposal]
the Policeman (Marc). The set calls it Station Guard: Marc to say which name.
so the first deck can fight [Proposal]
so the first deck can bring a shield back [Proposal]
so the first deck can mend [Proposal]

starter_pack.how: Fill the slots in order. In each slot, draw that many battle cards at random from those of its type and rarity. No card twice in one pack. The draw uses the child's own seed, so a child always gets the same pack and two children get different ones. The battle page does it in starterPack() (checks/battle_engine_test.js tests it on 10,000 seeds).
